transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

For weeks I’ve had this nonstop drive to take on more at the hospital, like I can’t slow my mind or body down even when I know it’s too much. It's just been really hard to control, and it's starting to cause some major problems for me.
Have you also experienced a period of feeling unusually low, hopeless, or depressed for most of the day, nearly every day, lasting at least two weeks?

Yes, since I crashed and got written up at work, I've had this heavy, sinking feeling every morning like there's no point in trying. This down phase has been dragging on for close to a month now, and it just sits on me all day.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [F30, F31, F43.1], but based on the current conversation, F30 (manic episode) is less likely because the patient reports both a distinct past period of increased drive and activity (manic-like symptoms) and a current prolonged depressive episode following a crash, which aligns more closely with a bipolar course. F43.1 (post-traumatic stress disorder) is no longer considered likely due to absence of trauma-related symptoms in the narrative. The presence of both elevated and depressive episodes supports F31 (bipolar affective disorder) as the only remaining candidate.
